essence: Change who you are becoming, and the habits follow.
modern_lens: Chapter 2 moves the focus from what you want to achieve to who you want to be. A manager who sees themselves as someone who gives clear feedback keeps doing it long after the training ends. Every small action is evidence, and enough evidence changes the story you tell about yourself.

ideas.name: Three Layers of Change
ideas.text: Change can target outcomes (what you get), processes (what you do) or identity (what you believe about yourself). Most plans start with outcomes. Habits last longer when they start from identity and work outward to process and results.
ideas.try: For one goal, write the outcome, the process and an identity sentence that starts with: I am the kind of person who.

ideas.name: Identity-Based Habits
ideas.text: A behaviour that conflicts with your self-image rarely lasts, however good the plan. Someone who is trying to quit still sees themselves as a smoker; someone who simply does not smoke has changed identity. Make the habit part of who you are.
ideas.try: Replace one 'I am trying to' sentence with an identity statement you can act on today.

ideas.name: Every Action Is a Vote
ideas.text: Each time you do the habit, you cast a vote for the person you want to become. You do not need every vote, only a majority. One workout does not make you fit, but it is evidence, and evidence builds belief.
ideas.try: Tonight, list three small votes you cast today for the person you want to be.

ideas.name: Decide, Then Prove It
ideas.text: Identity change is a two-step loop: decide what type of person you want to be, then prove it to yourself with small wins. In any moment, ask what that person would do here, and do the smallest version of it.
ideas.try: Before your next routine decision, ask what a reliable, healthy or generous person would do right now.

ideas.name: Loosen Limiting Labels
ideas.text: Beliefs such as being bad with numbers or not a morning person feel like facts, but they are often habits repeated for years. They protect your self-image and block change. Treat old labels as old evidence that new votes can outweigh.
ideas.try: Write one label that holds you back and one small action this week that contradicts it.
